statute: Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration & Protection) Act, 1999
title: Protection of Ayurvedic Botanicals and Formulations under Geographical Indications
content:
The GI Act provides community intellectual property rights identifying goods as originating in a specific geographical territory, where a given quality, reputation or other characteristic is essentially attributable to its geographical origin.

Ayurvedic Applications:
1. Registered Ayurvedic GIs: Navara Rice (medicinal rice used in Panchakarma), Alleppey Green Cardamom, Malabar Pepper, Erode Turmeric, Kandhamal Haldi, Nilambur Teak.
2. Legal Exclusivity: Only authorized users registered under Section 17 can market their produce with the registered GI tag.
3. Distinction from Patents: GI protects collective community heritage and regional reputation indefinitely (renewed every 10 years), preventing biopiracy and misleading origin labelling.
